nodes.label: DESI DR2 flat-LambdaCDM fit with mild BAO-CMB tension
nodes.summary: DESI reported that its DR2 BAO results were well described by a flat LambdaCDM model while the parameters preferred by BAO were in mild 2.3-sigma tension with those determined from the CMB.

nodes.label: DES Y6 reported weak preference for evolving dark energy
nodes.summary: The DES Collaboration reported that its analyzed probe combinations supported a weak preference for evolving dark energy, with the significance of deviation from a cosmological constant ranging from 2.3 to 3.2 sigma when individual probes were left out.

canonical_record.label: DESI DR2 flat-LambdaCDM fit with mild BAO-CMB tension
canonical_record.summary: DESI reported that its DR2 BAO results were well described by a flat LambdaCDM model while the parameters preferred by BAO were in mild 2.3-sigma tension with those determined from the CMB.

assertions.statement: DESI reported that its DR2 BAO results were well described by a flat LambdaCDM model while the parameters preferred by BAO were in mild 2.3-sigma tension with those determined from the CMB.

scope.population: The DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements and the cosmological parameter comparison described in the retained source.
scope.time: The retained source reports DESI DR2 results based on three years of operation; atlas chronology is left unresolved under era=undated.
scope.assumptions: The statement is conditional on the DESI DR2 BAO cosmological analysis and its comparison with CMB-determined parameters described by the collaboration.
scope.uncertainty: The source characterizes the tension as mild and does not establish that flat LambdaCDM is falsified or that a dynamical-dark-energy interpretation is uniquely correct.
scope.quantifiers: Restricted to the reported DESI DR2 BAO results and the stated 2.3-sigma BAO-CMB parameter tension.

support.quote: The results are well described by a flat $\Lambda$CDM model, but the parameters preferred by BAO are in mild, $2.3\sigma$ tension with those determined from the cosmic microwave background (CMB), although the DESI results are consistent with the acoustic angular scale $\theta_*$ that is well-measured by Planck.

canonical_record.label: DES Y6 reported weak preference for evolving dark energy
canonical_record.summary: The DES Collaboration reported that its analyzed probe combinations supported a weak preference for evolving dark energy, with the significance of deviation from a cosmological constant ranging from 2.3 to 3.2 sigma when individual probes were left out.

assertions.statement: The DES Collaboration reported that its analyzed probe combinations supported a weak preference for evolving dark energy, with the significance of deviation from a cosmological constant ranging from 2.3 to 3.2 sigma when individual probes were left out.

scope.population: The dark-energy probe combinations analyzed in the full six-year Dark Energy Survey study described by the retained source.
scope.time: The retained source reports the full six-year Dark Energy Survey analysis; atlas chronology is left unresolved under era=undated.
scope.assumptions: The analysis assumes a time-dependent dark-energy equation of state and uses the probe combinations and omission tests described by the DES Collaboration.
scope.uncertainty: The collaboration explicitly describes the result as a weak preference; the represented claim does not assert discovery of evolving dark energy or falsification of a cosmological constant.
scope.quantifiers: Restricted to the analyzed probe combinations in the retained source; the reported deviation significance spans 2.3 to 3.2 sigma across the stated leave-one-probe-out tests.

support.quote: We systematically investigate the impact of leaving out each one of the probes and find that the significance of the deviation from a cosmological constant ranges from 2.3 to 3.2$\sigma$, with best-fit parameters consistently in the region $w_0 >-1$ and $w_a <0$.
These results support the weak preference for evolving dark energy reported by several recent cosmological analyses.
